sampled.effective_real_interest_rate: triangular(low, central, high) from parameters.yaml macro inputs (C2)
sampled.gdp_deflator_growth: triangular(low, central, high) from parameters.yaml macro inputs (C2)
sampled.tfp_growth: triangular(low, central, high) from parameters.yaml macro inputs (C2)
sampled.human_capital_growth: triangular(low, central, high) from parameters.yaml macro inputs (C2)
sampled.investment_rate: triangular(low, central, high) from parameters.yaml macro inputs (C2)
sampled.okun_coefficient: triangular(low, central, high) from parameters.yaml macro inputs (C2)
sampled.pension_gdp_per_worker_weight: uniform(low, high), snapped to a 0.025 grid
sampled.sovereign_risk_bp: triangular(2, 5, 7) from long_run_feedback.sovereign_risk_premium; deviation vs base-year debt capped at 50 pp (choice)
sampled.revenue_elasticity: uniform(0.92, 0.98) from revenue_elasticity_to_gdp (IFI EE16 long run; C2 deterministic rule is 1.0)
sampled.leakage_share: uniform(low, high) from governance.leakage_share_of_spending (cancels in scenario-vs-S0 comparisons; drives the leakage_halved sensitivity)
sampled.firm_exit_rate_coefficient: normal(0.713, (1.512 + 0.085) / 3.92), separate stream [seed, 7]; imprecise, CI includes zero

corruption: G2 major-scandal shock: annual probability uniform(0.03, 0.08), GDP level loss triangular(1.0, 2.25, 3.6)%, 2-year build-up, 4-year recovery half-life; one event sequence per draw shared by every scenario and programme (stream [seed, 4]); included in external_gdp_level_pct and the *_with_external outputs
stock_flow_adjustment: Claude review (2026-10-23), following D2's Tier 2 FAIL: block bootstrap (3-year blocks) of the observed 2011-2024 implied stock-flow adjustment (D2 sfa_summary.values_by_year; dominated by discretionary Treasury<->BNDES loan operations and BCB result transfers, not predictable from covariates), demeaned so it adds historical-sized debt-level noise rather than a trend; one path per draw applied identically to every scenario (stream [seed, 9]), on top of any scenario-specific debt_adjustment_by_year (e.g. privatisation); included in debt_gdp, debt_gdp_with_external and debt_gdp_with_feedback. Not an exact cancellation in debt_gdp_vs_s0_pp over multiple years (each scenario's own GDP effect feeds the nominal-growth denominator of the debt recursion), but the shock does not favour any scenario. Does not change D2's historical backtest point-error, which is a separate, non-stochastic identity check.

fixed.point_inputs: every macro input with low = central = high (initial debt, revenue/GDP, capital share, K/Y, depreciation, GDP anchors)

external: C7 output channel: block bootstrap (3-year blocks) of joint 2001-2024 commodity export price, world growth (both demeaned) and BRL/USD changes, same path for every scenario in a draw (stream [seed, 1]); channel-A coefficient set drawn per draw from the two prespecified estimation windows (stream [seed, 3])
choices: triangular sampling for ranges is a modelling choice (fiscal_multipliers_brazil.sampling_rule), not a sourced distribution
parameters are sampled independently: no sourced correlations
persistence (transitory/persistent) is reported as a dimension, not sampled
percentiles describe parameter uncertainty only, not forecast error or external shocks
firm_distress: BK NPL and exit-rate indicators are associational and indicator-only; they do not feed back to GDP or debt. The exit-rate CI includes zero.
micro_outputs: C3 distribution indicators are changes versus S0; poverty outputs include all-person, age 0-14, age 65+, and people living with a 65+ pension/BPC recipient headcounts for both poverty lines

programmes.sampling: unstated sizes uniform over their ranges, T uniform over whole years 2-6; central run uses midpoints (T = 4)
programmes.status: unpublished until the D2 gate and lead/user review
